text: You ruled out changing this belief regardless of evidence. Try naming one observation that would make you reconsider, and what you would change.
You connected an expected outcome to a mechanism. That makes an important part of your view easier to inspect.
You identified something that could change your view. This is a useful crux to keep watching.
You made a condition or scope visible. That helps distinguish the expectation from the circumstances it depends on.
You expressed uncertainty in a way that leaves room for more evidence. That does not itself make the expected outcome better or worse.
You engaged with a serious reason your expectation might be wrong. The alternative is useful to inspect alongside your main account.
Your stated positions fit together under the conditions you described. That remains an interpretation of these answers.
You connected your account to evidence that could be checked. A reference still has limits on what it establishes.
You expect some benefits from AI and described limits or conditions in your account. Consider which of those conditions matter most for the gains you expect.
Harm is a consequential part of your expectation. This assessment keeps that expectation separate from your preferred response.
You expect technical control to be feasible under demanding conditions. Those conditions matter to the rest of the outlook.
You expect institutions to matter to what happens. The incentives and coordination in your account are worth examining.
You expect the forms of agency or continuity you value to be substantially preserved or expanded.
Your account includes how progress could unfold. Its timing and warning assumptions can affect both upside and risk.
You expressed a preferred response to AI. We keep that preference separate from the map’s expected-impact placement.
